title: Board Schedule: The Share of Production Allowed to Stand Sold Forward
content:
The ceiling percentage applied to a member's marketing average under Grain Marketing Contracts rises with what the member has marketed through the cooperative and with the standing of their equity account under Membership and Patronage Equity.

| The member's marketing and equity standing | Ceiling percentage |
|---|---|
| The bushels the equity ledger records the member marketing over the last thirty-six months reach 55000 and the equity account carries voting rights | 88.0 percent |
| The equity account stands active and the ledger records grain business inside the last twelve months, but that pair of conditions is not met | 78.0 percent |
| Neither of those holds | the share of production the member's marketing programme allows to stand sold forward |

## Reading the bands

The first band asks for both of its conditions together: 55000 bushels of marketed business over the last thirty-six months, the figure itself qualifying, and voting rights on the equity account. A member with 55000 bushels but no voting rights falls to the second band where their account stands active and grain business stands inside the last twelve months. A member with 54,999 bushels and voting rights falls there too. A member with no active equity account takes neither figure, and the percentage is the one their marketing programme carries.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

On a hypothetical marketing average of 50,000 bushels, a member with 61,000 bushels of marketed business over the last thirty-six months and a voting equity account has a ceiling of 44,000 bushels before the hauled-load credit and the forward reserve. The same average, on an active account without voting rights and with grain business inside the last twelve months, gives 39,000 bushels.
